key_insight: A physics-informed CNN-LSTM can forecast long-term photoluminescence degradation of unseen perovskite samples from early time-series data, enabling faster stability screening.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical route to reduce accelerated-aging experiment time and improve materials down-selection for perovskite solar cell development.
method: Collected 86k+ photoluminescence spectra from 167 metal-halide perovskites under heat and light stress
Physics-informed featurization converts spectra into interpretable stability descriptors
Hybrid CNN-LSTM forecasts future PL intensity for previously unseen samples and material groups
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a diverse dataset of 167 perovskites and >86k PL spectra, with the proposed model outperforming baseline benchmarks and generalizing across material groups.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality and coverage of the training dataset, so extrapolation to new chemistries or stress conditions should be validated carefully.
paper_title: Physics-informed time-series forecasting of perovskite photoluminescence stability
